rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Opening line (l.13) leads with the positive discipline — 'Plan mode is a permission state, not a feature' — and the close (l.62) leads with 'making the plan good IS the work.' 'Approval inflation' as a named failure mode is deliberately absent from the body (maintainer l.76), deferred to the exercise retro where it's earned. 'Three pressures that make bad plans look good' (l.39) is a sub-section naming reasoning traps to recognize, not the module's Big Idea, so it doesn't trip the rule's failure-as-title target.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity — consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, and mood-doesn't-resolve-early into one verdict.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Front-run check: maintainer block (l.76) confirms 'plan-mode approval inflation' stays withheld for the exercise's P5 retro; the fifth criterion's Horthy attribution is scoped to what non-goals mean for the plan, not a preview of a downstream skill reveal. Module-to-module arc: close ('Making the plan good IS the work... the execution can wait for the day the task is real,' l.62) hands off to the 'Push back on the plan' exercise, which reuses this lecture's exact vocabulary (file list / early runnable slice / verification step / named assumptions / non-goals, 'you will notice the wait') as its own opening language. Big Idea fidelity: the lecture's opening frame — plan mode as a permission state producing a reviewable artifact, not a feeling — matches the deck notes' framing of the module's central move. Mood doesn't resolve early: the close stays in grounded-competence register without tipping into the felt payoff ('is-me' rating stays at 8, not a resolved 10) the exercise is about to deliver — it names the discipline, doesn't yet demonstrate having lived it.
